- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model overestimates recovery — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate mean reversion — reduce forecast by 3–7% if recent 7-day avg is above 30-day moving avg.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to recognize it — add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly down, model overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ days.
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in sentiment-driven periods — reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment swings >0.5 in 3-day window.
